title: Solubility Product (Ksp) Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Salt vanishes in water, chalk dust just sinks, and an old kettle grows a white crust. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Diya stirs chalk into water and we ask how much of a solid water can really hold.

You will see the three solubility classes (above 0.1 M, 0.01 to 0.1 M, below 0.01 M), then watch barium sulphate ions leave and rejoin the solid on the molecule bench until the solution is saturated. We define the solubility product Ksp (BaSO4: 1.1 x 10^-10 at 298 K, s = 1.05 x 10^-5 mol/L), link Ksp to solubility s for AB (Ksp = s^2) and AB2 (Ksp = 4s^3) salts, show the common ion effect live, compare the ionic product Q with Ksp to predict a precipitate, solve a worked example in pure water and with a common ion, show the squaring trap, then an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 70 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
